sections.name: Full-bleed roofing hero, parallax image + staggered headline
sections.notes: Fixed-position hero image creates a parallax effect as the page scrolls under it (JS toggles .is-past once scrolled out of the viewport — not included here, degrades gracefully to a static bg). Headline lines and CTAs fade/slide in via .intro-in class added on load; .no-js fallback keeps everything visible with no JS. Image path is a placeholder — swap in your own asset.

sections.name: Draggable horizontal review carousel with reply cards
sections.notes: Real Google reviews for a live client, kept verbatim as a content pattern reference (swap in the target business's own reviews before reuse). The reply line under each card — owner responding by name — is the standout trust device here; worth reusing even without the carousel. Horizontal scroll uses a CSS mask to fade the edges instead of hard-clipping cards; JS drag-to-scroll (grab/grabbing cursor) not included but the CSS supports it as pure scroll-snap too.

sections.name: Featured-service spotlight + compact grid of secondary services
sections.notes: Two-tier services pattern: one large 'specialty' feature card (image + long copy + capability list + link to its own page) alongside a compact grid of the remaining services as smaller cards. Good reference whenever a business has one flagship service worth showcasing and several supporting ones that don't need equal real estate.

sections.name: Split hero with rotating slide gallery and botanical line-art accents
sections.notes: Copy sits left, a fading slideshow of portrait-orientation photos sits right — good pattern for photographers/creatives where the images ARE the pitch. Inline SVG botanical sprigs (referenced via <use href="#bot-...">) are decorative flourishes defined once in a sprite sheet elsewhere on the page; this fragment references them by id but doesn't include the sprite defs. Uses <picture>/srcset for responsive art direction.

sections.name: Segmented pricing packages by client type (tiers within categories)
sections.notes: Not a single price ladder — instead groups by WHO the client is (Families, Solos & Graduates, etc.) and shows 1-2 price tiers inside each group. Good reference for service businesses whose pricing varies more by customer segment than by feature tier. data-reveal attributes hook into an intersection-observer fade-in (script not included).

sections.name: Split hero with trust badge, overlapping stat card, and plank texture accent
sections.notes: Stat card (years in business / review count / rating) overlaps the hero image corner rather than living in its own section — keeps proof visible without adding vertical scroll. data-count-to attributes are hooks for a count-up-on-scroll script (not included, degrades to static numbers). No webfont dependency — deliberately system-font for a fast, plain-spoken feel matching the trade.

sections.name: Minimal centered dark CTA banner
sections.notes: About as simple as a closing CTA gets: headline, one line of support copy, a phone-call button and a secondary quote-request button. Useful as a mid-page or pre-footer breather section when a full contact form section would be too heavy. Smallest file in the library — good starting point to restyle rather than strip down.

sections.name: Full-bleed hero with animated line-by-line headline and live open/closed status
sections.notes: Three one-word headline lines ('Climbed.' 'Cut.' 'Cleared.') each animate in on their own line — punchy rhythm pattern worth reusing for trades with a clear step-by-step process. Has a commented-out slot for swapping the still image for a looping background video once the client supplies footage. data-status/data-status-text hooks are for a live business-hours widget (JS not included, static fallback text shown as-is).

sections.name: Combined proof section: animated stat row + award plaque + Google rating summary
sections.notes: Stacks three proof devices in one section instead of spreading them thin: a stat row (years/reviews/rating/awards, count-up-on-scroll hooks via data-count), a photographed award plaque with a bulleted achievement list, and a Google-rating summary block (real G logo SVG inlined) with an HTML comment marking where to drop in a live Elfsight/Trustindex/Featurable review-widget embed later. Heaviest file in the library — good candidate to split back into 2-3 smaller sections if only one device is needed.

sections.name: Luxury full-bleed hero with badge, glow overlay, and location pin
sections.notes: Layers a subtle radial 'glow' div over the standard image+gradient hero for extra shine — cheap way to make a dark hero feel premium/detailing-shop rather than flat. HTML comment marks exactly what the hero image should be before an asset existed yet, worth keeping as a habit when spec-building ahead of client photos.

sections.name: Simple centered CTA banner with label tag and phone/book buttons
sections.notes: Same job as 0007 (Denton Fence CTA) but with a small uppercase label-tag above the headline and .fade-up scroll-reveal hooks — compare the two side by side for 'plain trade CTA' vs 'polished premium-service CTA' at nearly the same structure.
